status.en: 79 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 34% fewer than the week before, most of them in Islamabad, Kabul and Peshawar.
status.nb: 79 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 34 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Islamabad, Kabul og Peshawar.

summary.en: Arrests continue as Peshawar ATC reissued an arrest warrant for Sohail Afridi in the Radio Pakistan attack, while police faced lethal attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, with eleven police personnel feared killed in one incident and twelve injured in another in Kohat. Strikes by lawyers oppose the suspension of provincial health commission powers, and a general strike by Spaniards reflects broader unrest but is unrelated to the local conflict. The conflict still accounts for 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Arrestasjonene fortsetter ettersom Peshawar ATC har utstedt en ny arrestordre mot Sohail Afridi i Radio Pakistan-angrepet, mens politiet ble utsatt for dødelige angrep i Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, med elleve politifolk antatt drept i én hendelse og tolv sårede i en annen i Kohat. Advokater streiker mot suspensjon av provinsens helsekommisjons fullmakter, og en landsomfattende streik blant spanjoler reflekterer bredere uro men er ikke knyttet til den lokale konflikten. Konflikten står fortsatt for 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
